newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen stocks dive at noon on crackdown talk.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen stocks dive at noon on crackdown talk.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B shares plunged on Wednesday at midday as talk of a possible government crackdown on China's stock markets gained momentum, analysts said.
The foreign currency B share index plunged 6.03 points or 3.38 percent to end the morning at 172.33 on turnover of HK$40.2 million.
The domestic currency A index dropped 25.51 points or 4.80 percent to 506.01 on turnover of 6.2 billion yuan.
"People think the government is really going to turn the markets upside-down," an analyst at J&A Securities said.
Rumors swirled in the Shanghai and Shenzhen markets that the securities authorities may suspend the trading licenses of several major brokerages for alleged market manipulation, analysts said.
"It is beginning to look like the authorities may strip us of our license very soon," a trader at a major domestic brokerage said.
A Hong Kong newspaper said on Tuesday that Chinese authorities will no longer tolerate the recent "crazy" gains in share prices, and will soon announce measures to clampdown on the stock market.
Traders said rumours centred on a possible extension of the transaction settlement period to three days for both A and B shares in a bid to reduce market volatility.
This compares with the current settlement period of one day for A shares and immediate settlement for B shares, analysts said.
"Despite widespread talk about a settlement extension, I do not think it will be as long as three days since this would stall the market," an analyst at Central-South Securities said.
The A and B indices are likely to continue to slip lower in the afternoon in nervous trading, analysts said.
"Trading volumes are thin, indicating investor reluctance to bet on the market," an analyst at a major brokerage said.
Shenzhen Health Mineral Water Co Ltd was the worst performer in the B share market, losing HK$0.33 or 7.62 percent to HK$4.00.
The star performer was Chiwan Wharf Holdings Ltd, which on Wednesday said it would build a cargo warehouse with a Hong Kong company. Chiwan rose HK$0.05 or 0.94 percent to HK$5.35.
